Other details: None

new.summary: You further develop your ability to listen to, understand, speak, read and write Sesotho. The course also introduces basic cultural issues related to the Sesotho way of life and misunderstandings in intercultural communication.

covers.courses/SLL1029F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 247 (Language options row 6)
covers.courses/SLL1029S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 247 (Language options row 7)

rows.printed:
SLL1029F Language and Cross-Cultural Communication
Course outline: This course is an introduction to communication and culture in African languages. Whereas the main
focus is on the South African indigenous languages, classroom activities will require students to draw
from their living experiences to understand cross-cultural communication. As an introductory course,
we use content that engages the diversity of students’ life worlds and is cognisant of our African
location. We employ innovative teaching and delivery methods, including multilingual pedagogies
and digital literacy, which allow more time for active engagement and the development of critical
reading and writing skills in the Humanities.
Entry requirements: Not stated in course entry.
Class times: Arranged by the Section.
Assessment: Continuous assessment (essays, class tests, projects) counts 100%.

DP requirements: Attendance of all tutorials and completion of all written work.
Other details: This course may also be offered in Winter Term - please consult the Faculty.

new.summary: Explore African-language communication and culture, focusing on South African indigenous languages and cross-cultural exchange grounded in students’ lived experiences. You’ll use multilingual and digital approaches while developing critical reading and writing skills.

covers.courses/SLL1042F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 254 (Language options row 16)
covers.courses/SLL1042S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 254 (Language options row 17)

rows.printed:
SLL1042F Afrikaans Intensive A
Course outline: The course enables students with no prior knowledge of Afrikaans to develop a basic competency in
the language, which is required for basic daily interactions. Afrikaans grammar is taught within
context, appropriate vocabulary is systematically expanded and a variety of relevant written and oral
activities are provided to facilitate comprehension.
Entry requirements: None. This is a course for beginners; under certain conditions students
with basic knowledge of Afrikaans may be permitted to attend, with permission of the Section Head.
Class times: Monday to Friday 4th period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination in June or October/November counts for 40% of the final
mark; an oral examination counts for 20%; the semester coursework counts for the remaining 40%.

DP requirements: At least 75% attendance at lectures; completion of all assignments and tests.
Other details: None

new.summary: This course builds basic Afrikaans skills for everyday interactions, introducing grammar in context and systematically expanding vocabulary. Through written and oral activities, students develop comprehension and a beginner’s ability to use the language.

covers.courses/SLL1050F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 264 (Language options row 22)

rows.printed:
SLL1050F Latin IA
Course outline: The course provides an introduction to Latin for students with no previous knowledge of Latin. It
offers insights into word formation and sentence structure and the Latin roots of common words in
English. The syllabus includes a selection of prose passages, and a study of translation from English
into Latin.
Entry requirements: None. This course is primarily designed for those who have not studied
Latin before, but is also open to those who have done some Latin at school but not enough to enter
Latin IB or IIA.
Class times: Monday to Friday 7th period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination in June counts for 50% of the final mark; coursework counts
50%.

DP requirements: Students will not be permitted to write the examination unless they have submitted
all coursework.
Other details: None

new.summary: Learn the basics of Latin, including how words are formed, how sentences are structured, and how Latin roots appear in common English words. You will read prose passages and practise translating English into Latin.

covers.courses/SLL1051S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 264 (Language options row 23)

rows.printed:
SLL1051S Latin IB
Course outline: The course builds on Latin IA and provides further instruction in Latin vocabulary, grammar and
syntax (including complex sentences and subordinate clauses – temporal, concessive, final,
consecutive, oratio obliqua), and includes introductory study of a selection of continuous prose
passages, and practice in translation of complex sentences from English into Latin.
Entry requirements: SLL1050F Latin IA
Class times: Monday to Friday 7th period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination in October/November counts for 50% of the final mark;
coursework counts 50%.

DP requirements: Students will not be permitted to write the examination unless they have submitted
all coursework.
Other details: None

new.summary: Builds on introductory Latin with more vocabulary, grammar and syntax, including complex sentences and subordinate clauses. You’ll read selected passages of continuous prose and practise translating complex English sentences into Latin.

covers.courses/SLL1052F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 266 (Language options row 24)

rows.printed:
SLL1052F Greek IA
Course outline: This course is designed for students with no previous knowledge of Ancient Greek. It provides an
introduction to basic grammar and syntax, and a basic working vocabulary. A great emphasis is placed
in graded reading of passages in Greek and gradual introduction of idioms of Classical Greek prose.
Aspects of Ancient Greek culture and historical context are included where relevant.
Entry requirements: None
Class times: Monday to Friday 8th period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination in June counts for 40% of the final mark; coursework counts
for 60%.

DP requirements: Submission of all coursework, write all tests and 80% lecture attendance.
Other details: None

new.summary: You will learn basic Ancient Greek grammar, syntax and vocabulary through graded reading, with a gradual introduction to idioms of Classical Greek prose. The course also introduces Ancient Greek culture and historical context where relevant.

covers.courses/SLL1053S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 266 (Language options row 25)

rows.printed:
SLL1053S Greek IB
Course outline: The course builds on Greek IA and provides further instruction in Greek vocabulary, grammar and
syntax (including complex sentences and subordinate clauses – temporal, concessive, final,
consecutive, indirect statement). The reading passages become gradually more complex and are based
increasingly on actual surviving Greek examples of dramatic comedy and forensic oratory. There is
increased practice in translating English into Greek, and Greek into English.
Entry requirements: SLL1052F Greek IA
Class times: 8th period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination in October/November counts for 40% of the final mark;
coursework counts for 60%.

DP requirements: Submission of all coursework, write all tests and 80% lecture attendance.
Other details: None

new.summary: Students extend Greek vocabulary, grammar and syntax, including complex sentences and subordinate clauses. They read increasingly complex passages from surviving comedy and forensic oratory, and practise translating between English and Greek.

corrected.summary: Extend your Greek vocabulary, grammar and syntax, including complex sentences and subordinate clauses. Read increasingly complex passages from real Greek comedies and courtroom speeches, and practise translating between English and Greek.

covers.courses/SLL1054F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 268 (Courses row 64)

rows.printed:
SLL1054F The World of Odysseus
Course outline: This course provides an introduction to the ancient Mediterranean world through Homer's Odyssey,
examining the hero, Odysseus, in the context of early Greek society and its oral traditions, and tracing
the hero's fortunes in ancient and modern literature, film and art. All texts are studied in English, and
no knowledge of ancient languages is required.
Entry requirements: None
Class times: Monday to Thursday 6th period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination in June counts for 50% of the final mark; coursework counts
for 50%.

DP requirements: Students must attend classes regularly, submit the prescribed number of essays
and assignments and write any class test that may be scheduled. Submission dates must be adhered to.
Other details: None

new.summary: Explore the ancient Mediterranean through Homer's Odyssey, considering Odysseus as a hero shaped by early Greek society and oral traditions. Trace his changing fortunes across ancient and modern literature, film and art.

covers.courses/SLL1057F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 268 (Courses row 65)

rows.printed:
SLL1057F Ancient Egypt
Course outline: This course provides students with no previous knowledge of ancient history with an introduction to
(i) the history of Egypt from c. 4000 BC to AD 300, and (ii) key elements of Egyptian culture
(including architecture and religion). The course will consider how Egyptian culture adapted to rule
by foreign powers (Greek and Roman) and how these foreigners perceived and represented Egypt. As
an introductory course, we use content that engages the diversity of students' lifeworlds and is
cognizant of our African location. We employ innovative teaching and delivery methods that allow
more time for active engagement and the development of critical reading and writing skills in the
Humanities.
Entry requirements: None
Class times: Monday, Wednesday, Friday 3rd period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination in June counts for 50% of the final mark; coursework counts
for 50%.

DP requirements: Students must attend classes regularly, submit the prescribed number of essays
and assignments and write any class test that may be scheduled. Submission dates must be adhered to.
Other details: None

new.summary: Study Egyptian history from about 4000 BC to AD 300, including architecture, religion, and adaptation to Greek and Roman rule. Examine foreign views of Egypt and build critical reading and writing skills through active learning.

covers.courses/SLL1058F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 256 (Language options row 18)

rows.printed:
SLL1058F Initial Arabic A
Course outline: The course provides students with their first steps in both written and spoken Modern Standard Arabic.
The first weeks are taken up with studying the alphabet and the writing and pronunciation rules along
with some basics of conversation. In the following part of the course students are introduced to the
structure of nominal and verbal sentences, conjugation of past tense, use of demonstratives and other
basics.
Entry requirements: None
Class times: Monday to Friday 8th period.
Assessment: Written and oral assignments and tests count for 40% of the final mark; the two-hour
written examination at the end of the first semester counts for 50%; the oral examination at the end of
the semester counts for 10%.

DP requirements: At least 80% attendance at lectures, seminars and tutorials (including language
laboratory where offered); completion and due submission of all written exercises and essays;
attendance at all tests, written and oral examinations.
Other details: None

new.summary: Students take their first steps in spoken and written Modern Standard Arabic, learning its alphabet, writing and pronunciation rules alongside basic conversation. They then study sentence structures, past-tense conjugation and demonstratives as foundations for using the language.

covers.courses/SLL1059S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 257 (Language options row 19)

rows.printed:
SLL1059S Initial Arabic B
Course outline: This course continues from Arabic IA in offering a beginners’ level study of Modern Standard Arabic
with emphasis on oral comprehension and communication along with writing and reading skills. The
students are taught the plural of nouns and demonstratives, conjugation of present tense, derived forms
of verbs and other elements of grammar, while texts and exercises will also provide them with a large
amount of useful vocabulary.
Entry requirements: Initial Arabic A (SLL1058F)
Class times: Monday to Friday 8th period.
Assessment: Written and oral assignments and tests count for 40% of the final mark; the two-hour
written examination at the end of the second semester counts for 50%; the oral examination at the end
of the semester counts for 10%.

DP requirements: At least 80% attendance at lectures, seminars and tutorials (including language
laboratory where offered); completion and due submission of all written exercises and essays;
attendance at all tests, written and oral examinations.
Other details: None

new.summary: Continue developing Modern Standard Arabic through practice in listening, speaking, reading and writing. Learn useful vocabulary and grammar, including noun plurals, demonstratives, present-tense conjugation and derived verb forms for communication.

covers.courses/SLL1060F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 273 (Language options row 26)

rows.printed:
SLL1060F French Intensive A
Course outline: This course offers an intensive introduction to French as a foreign language focusing on the basic
grammatical, lexical, phonetic, and cultural aspects of the language. The course aims to equip students
with a thorough understanding of the structure of the language for further study, all the while acquiring
reading, writing, listening and speaking skills for communication purposes.
Entry requirements: None. This is a course for beginners. Students with previous knowledge
of French may not register for this course.
Class times: Monday to Friday either in 2nd or 5th period and one conversation class per week.
Assessment: Students are evaluated by continuous assessment (80% of the final mark) and an end-
of-semester oral examination (20% of final mark).

DP requirements: Completion of class tests and oral examinations on the date indicated, submission
of all assignments by the due date, and minimum of 80% attendance of all sections of the course are
compulsory for the Duly Performed Certificate.
Other details: This course may also be offered in Winter Term – please consult the Department.

new.summary: An intensive beginner course introduces French grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation and culture, while developing reading, writing, listening and speaking skills for communication. You gain a grounding in its structure for further study and communication in French.

covers.courses/SLL1061S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 273 (Language options row 27)

rows.printed:
SLL1061S French Intensive B
Course outline: This course offers a further intensive introduction to French as a foreign language focusing on the
basic grammatical, lexical, phonetic, and cultural aspects of the language. The course aims to equip
students with a thorough understanding of the structure of the language for further study, all the while
acquiring reading, writing, listening and speaking skills for communication purposes.
Entry requirements: SLL1060F or equivalent. This second semester is specially designed
for students who passed SLL1060F but students with adequate level of French language acquisition
may, by permission of the course convener, be admitted in SLL1061S. Note that “special admissions”
exclude students coming from countries where French is spoken and/or taught; thus students who have
studied French at high school, e.g. South Africa, Zimbabwe, and/or passed their Matric – with French
as a foreign language - within the last three years at the day of registration are not allowed to register
for this module.
Class times: Monday to Friday either in 2nd or 5th period and one conversation class per week.
Assessment: Students are evaluated by continuous assessment (80% of the final mark) and an end-
of-semester oral examination (20% of final mark).

DP requirements: Completion of class tests and oral examinations on the dated indicated, submission
of all assignments by the due date, and minimum of 80% attendance of all sections of the course are
compulsory for the Duly Performed Certificate.
Other details: None

new.summary: Builds on basic French with intensive study of grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation and culture. You develop an understanding of French structure alongside reading, writing, listening and speaking skills for communication and further study.

covers.courses/SLL1062F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 278 (Language options row 29)

rows.printed:
SLL1062F German Studies IA
Course outline: This course offers an introduction to German as a Foreign Language and German Studies focusing on
the basics of German language, comprehension of texts, and reflecting on selected cultural patterns.
An overview of German grammar and structure is given, which is supplemented by working with
basic texts. The course cultivates a basic understanding of everyday communicative skills in German.
Based on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), level A1 is aimed
for.
Entry requirements: No previous knowledge of German is required. Students who have
passed German within the preceding five years with at least a D symbol (SC), or a 4 rating (NSC), or
a course recognised as equivalent will not be admitted to this course for degree purposes unless the
Head of Section is satisfied that for some special reason they are not able to perform the work of
SLL2062F.
Class times: Monday to Friday 5th period.
Assessment: Coursework (homework and tests) counts for 40% of the final mark; two-hour written
examination counts for 40%; Language laboratory examination counts for 20%.

DP requirements: At least 80% attendance at lectures, seminars and tutorials (including the language
laboratory); completion and due submission of all written exercises and essays; attendance at all tests,
written and oral examinations.
Other details: This course may also be offered in Winter Term – please consult the Department.

new.summary: This course introduces basic German grammar, text comprehension and selected cultural patterns, aiming for CEFR A1. You develop everyday communicative skills in German and a basic understanding of the language through work with introductory texts.

covers.courses/SLL1063S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 279 (Language options row 30)

rows.printed:
SLL1063S German Studies IB
Course outline: Building on German IA, this course offers a continued introduction to German as a Foreign Language
and German Studies focusing on furthering an understanding of the basics of the German language,
consolidating the comprehension of texts, and reflecting on selected cultural patterns. A deeper
overview of German grammar and structures is given, which is supplemented by working with a wider
variety of texts. The course cultivates an understanding of everyday communicative skills and fosters
an ability to engage with specific topics in German. Based on the Common European Framework of
Reference for Languages (CEFR), level A2 is aimed for.
Entry requirements: Students must have passed SLL1062F. In certain instances, where
students have some informal knowledge of German, they may be admitted to German Studies IB
without having done German Studies IA, provided the Head of Section is satisfied of the students’
German competence. Students who have passed German within the preceding five years with at least
a D symbol (SC), or a 4 rating (NSC), or a course recognised as equivalent, will not be admitted to
this course for degree purposes unless the Head of Section is satisfied that for some special reason
they are not able to perform the work of SLL2062F.
Class times: Monday to Friday 5th period.
Assessment: Coursework (homework and tests) counts for 40% of the final mark; Two-hour written
examination counts for 40%; Language laboratory examination counts for 10%; Oral examination
counts for 10%.

DP requirements: At least 80% attendance at lectures, seminars and tutorials (including the language
laboratory); completion and due submission of all written exercises and essays; attendance at all tests,
written and oral examinations.
Other details: None

new.summary: Building on introductory German, the course deepens grammar and uses varied texts to strengthen comprehension and explore cultural patterns. You develop everyday communication skills and practise discussing topics in German, aiming for CEFR A2.

covers.courses/SLL1064F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 284 (Language options row 33)

rows.printed:
SLL1064F Italian Intensive A
Course outline: This course is intended for those who do not have any knowledge of Italian and consists of basic
grammar, vocabulary, grammar drill, oral practice and simple reading passages. The course also
consists of weekly language lab sessions and exercises and exposure to Italian culture by the
occasional screening and discussion of films.
Entry requirements: None. Students with a pass (SC) or a 4 rating (NSC) or equivalent in
Italian or mother-tongue speakers may be admitted directly into SLL2064F at the Head of Section's
discretion.
Class times: Monday to Friday 6th period.
Assessment: Written and oral assignments and tests count for 80% of the final mark; the 15-minute
oral examination at the end of the semester counts for 20%.

DP requirements: At least 80% attendance at lectures, seminars and tutorials (including language
laboratory where offered); completion and due submission of all written exercises and essays;
attendance at all tests, written and oral examinations.
Other details: None

new.summary: Beginners learn basic Italian through grammar, vocabulary, drills, oral practice and simple reading passages, with weekly language-lab sessions and exercises. Occasional film screenings and discussions introduce aspects of Italian culture.

covers.courses/SLL1065S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 284 (Language options row 34)

rows.printed:
SLL1065S Italian Intensive B
Course outline: This course is a continuation of the first semester course introducing students to more advanced
grammar, and thereby enabling them to gain a complete knowledge of the structure of the language.
This course also equips students to be able to cope with the second year Italian literature, language
and history.
Entry requirements: SLL1064F
Class times: Monday to Friday 6th period.
Assessment: Written and oral assignments and tests count for 80% of the final mark; the 15-minute
oral examination at the end of the semester counts for 20%.

DP requirements: At least 80% attendance at lectures, seminars and tutorials (including language
laboratory where offered); completion and due submission of all written exercises and essays;
attendance at all tests, written and oral examinations.
Other details: None

new.summary: Students continue from the first-semester course, studying more advanced Italian grammar to develop a complete understanding of the language’s structure. The course prepares them to cope with second-year Italian literature, language and history.

covers.courses/SLL1068F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 290 (Language options row 37)
covers.courses/SLL1068S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 290 (Language options row 38)

rows.printed:
SLL1068F Latin America: Texts and Artistic Representations
Course outline: Focusing on literary texts as well as the visual and performing arts, this course introduces the cultures
of Mexico, the Caribbean Islands, and Central and South America – a region known as Latin America.
Culturally diverse, Latin America is an important part of humanity's past and future; its histories,
politics, pieces of literature, and arts are a stimulating complement for a diversity of academic
disciplines and programmes. Topics covered in this survey course include the Aztec, Maya, and Inca
civilizations; European colonization; native music and dance; African diasporic cultural systems;
Amazonian ritual landscapes; etc. The reading material for this course is translated into English and
derives from texts written originally in Portuguese, Spanish, French, and Creole. No previous
knowledge or familiarity with the cultural and linguistic background of the studied regions is required.
The course is taught in English.
Entry requirements: None
Class times: Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, 7th period, plus one tutorial.
Assessment: Continuous assessment (essays, projects, tests, etc.) counts 100%.

DP requirements: At least 80% of attendance at lectures and tutorials; completion and timeous
submission of all assignments.
Other details: This course may also be offered in Summer Term – please consult the Department.

new.summary: Explore Latin American cultures through literature, visual art and performance, with material from Mexico, the Caribbean, Central and South America. Study Indigenous civilizations, colonization, music and dance, African diasporic cultures and ritual landscapes.

covers.courses/SLL1069F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 273–274 (Language options row 28)

rows.printed:
SLL1069F French Communication
Course outline: This course offers an introduction to French as a foreign language with a focus on the basic structures
of the language for communication purposes. Students will acquire practical knowledge of, notably,
spoken but also written French, leading up to the A1 level according to the Common European
Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). This is a stand-alone elective course that does not
automatically allow continuation to a second semester French course. However, if a student decides
they wish to take the second semester course and continue with French, they may take the winter term
SLL1060L French Intensive A course, which should be passed prior to continuing with SLL1061S
French Intensive B.
Entry requirements: None
Class times: 2nd and 5th Lectures Mon-Wed & Tutorials Thu-Fri.
Assessment: Continuous assessment (80%) and an oral exam (20%).

DP requirements: 80% attendance, handing in of all assignments and tests throughout the semester.
Other details: None

new.summary: This course introduces basic French structures for everyday communication, with an emphasis on speaking and some written French. You develop practical skills towards A1 level, as defined by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

covers.courses/SLL1073F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 290 (Language options row 39)

rows.printed:
SLL1073F Initial Spanish A
Course outline: The course is an intensive introductory language course, which aims to provide a practical knowledge
of spoken and written Spanish for beginners. The module targets to bring students up to a standard
where they can communicate and understand basic ideas in any variety of Spanish. The focus during
this first semester is on the introduction of Spanish grammar structures and vocabulary, and the
development of language skills in reading, writing and listening.
Entry requirements: None. This is a course for beginners, but under certain circumstances
students with prior knowledge of Spanish may be admitted.
Class times: Monday to Friday 8th period.
Assessment: Students are evaluated by continuous assessment (80% of the final mark) and an end-
of-semester oral examination (20% of final mark).

DP requirements: At least 80% attendance at lectures, tutorials and language laboratory sessions;
completion and timeous submission of all written assignments; attendance at all scheduled tests,
written and oral examinations.
Other details: None

new.summary: This intensive introductory course builds practical spoken and written Spanish through grammar, vocabulary, and practice in reading, writing, and listening. You develop skills to communicate and understand basic ideas across varieties of Spanish.

covers.courses/SLL1074S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 290–291 (Language options row 40)

rows.printed:
SLL1074S Initial Spanish B
Course outline: The course is a continuation of SLL1073F and aims to provide a further practical knowledge of spoken
and written Spanish of approximately Matriculation standard. There is no in-depth study of literature
at this level. The module focuses on the consolidation of language skills in reading, writing and
listening, and the introduction of conversational skills. By the end of this second semester, students
should be able to engage in interactions with Spanish speakers in socially and culturally appropriate
forms without problems.
Entry requirements: SLL1073F, or equivalent at the discretion of the Head of Department.
Class times: Monday to Friday 8th period.
Assessment: Students are evaluated by continuous assessment (80% of the final mark) and an end-
of-semester oral examination (20% of final mark).

DP requirements: At least 80% attendance at lectures, tutorials, and language laboratory sessions;
completion and timeous submission of all written assignments; attendance at all scheduled tests,
written and oral examinations.
Other details: None

new.summary: This course builds practical spoken and written Spanish through reading, writing and listening practice, while introducing conversation. Students develop the skills to interact with Spanish speakers in socially and culturally appropriate ways.

covers.courses/SLL1075F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 287 (Language options row 35)

rows.printed:
SLL1075F Initial Portuguese A
Course outline: The objective of this course is the development of proficiency in Portuguese at beginner’s level, with
a focus on practical knowledge and the acquisition of basic listening, speaking, reading, and writing
skills. It also offers an introduction to the cultures of the Portuguese-speaking countries.
Entry requirements: None. This is a course for beginners, but under certain circumstances
students with prior knowledge of Portuguese may be admitted.
Class times: Monday to Friday 1st period or meridian. Plus, one tutorial and one conversation class.
Assessment: Coursework 80%; end-of-semester oral examination 20%.

DP requirements: At least 80% attendance at lectures, tutorials and language laboratory sessions;
completion and timeous submission of all written assignments; attendance at all scheduled tests.
Other details: None

new.summary: Build proficiency in Portuguese at beginner level through practical work in listening, speaking, reading and writing, with a focus on acquiring basic language skills. Gain an introduction to the cultures of Portuguese-speaking countries.

covers.courses/SLL1076S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 287 (Language options row 36)

rows.printed:
SLL1076S Initial Portuguese B
Course outline: This course forms the continuation of Initial Portuguese A. Its objective is the further development of
proficiency in Portuguese at beginner’s level, with a focus on practical knowledge and on the
acquisition of basic listening, speaking, reading and writing skills. It also offers an introduction to the
cultures, of the Portuguese-speaking countries.
Entry requirements: SLL1075F, or equivalent at the discretion of the Head of Section.
Class times: Monday to Friday 1st period or meridian. Plus, one tutorial and one conversation class.
Assessment: Coursework 80%; end-of-semester oral examination 20%.

DP requirements: At least 80% attendance at lectures, tutorials and conversation classes; completion
and timeous submission of all written assignments; attendance at all scheduled tests.
Other details: None

new.summary: Building on Initial Portuguese A, the course develops beginner-level Portuguese through practical learning and basic listening, speaking, reading and writing skills. Students also gain an introduction to the cultures of Portuguese-speaking countries.

covers.courses/SLL1082F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 282 (Language options row 31)

rows.printed:
SLL1082F Hebrew Intensive A
Course outline: The course introduces students to the Hebrew alphabet and its unique vowel-system. Students gain
basic skills in reading, writing and conversation. A variety of verb forms are introduced in present and
past tenses, and with vocabulary of modern life it allows the students to express themselves, and join
in Hebrew conversation.
Entry requirements: None. The course is designed for those who have not studied Hebrew
before. In special cases students with an elementary knowledge of Hebrew may be admitted into the
course by special permission of the Head of Department. NOTE: Students who have passed SC or
NSC Hebrew or equivalent within the last five years are not eligible for registration.
Class times: 5th period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination counts 50% of the final mark; the remaining 50% is awarded
for classwork (35%) and oral (15%).

DP requirements: Students must attend regularly, prepare adequately for language classes and
tutorials and submit the prescribed number of written assignments, and write any class tests.
Other details: None

new.summary: Students learn the Hebrew alphabet and its distinctive vowel system, building basic reading, writing and conversation skills. They practise present and past verb forms and modern-life vocabulary to express themselves in Hebrew.

covers.courses/SLL1083S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 282 (Language options row 32)

rows.printed:
SLL1083S Hebrew Intensive B
Course outline: The course focuses on Hebrew grammar, vocabulary, conversation, reading and writing skills as it
builds on the basic skills of semester one. Students learn to distinguish between various linguistic
registers, as well as the various Hebrew styles from Biblical, to Rabbinic Hebrew to Modernity.
Though the course concentrates on Modern Hebrew it prepares the students to join Hebrew 2A –
where they need to analyse Hebrew Literature.
Entry requirements: SLL1082F or equivalent by permission of the Head of Department.
Class times: 5th period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination counts 50% of the final mark; the remaining 50% is awarded
for classwork (35%) and oral (15%).

DP requirements: As for SLL1082F.
Other details: None

new.summary: You build Hebrew skills through grammar, vocabulary, conversation, reading and writing, focusing on Modern Hebrew. You learn to distinguish registers and styles from Biblical and Rabbinic Hebrew to modern usage, preparing for Hebrew literature analysis.

covers.courses/SLL1097S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 268 (Courses row 66)

rows.printed:
SLL1097S Introducing Ancient History
Course outline: An introduction to the study of ancient history and classical archaeology in the Mediterranean world
from the 8th century BC to the early Roman Empire (1st century AD). The focus is on the development
of Rome in the Italian peninsula and the emergence of Rome as a major power in the Mediterranean
world. The reigns of the early Roman emperors are also covered.
Entry requirements: None
Class times: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 4th period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination in October/November counts for 50% of the final mark;
coursework counts for 50%.

DP requirements: Students must attend at least 80% of tutorials, submit the prescribed number of
essays and assignments and write any class test that may be scheduled. Submission dates must be
adhered to.
Other details: None

new.summary: Study ancient history and classical archaeology in the Mediterranean from the eighth century BC to early Roman imperial rule, tracing Rome's rise and its first emperors. It offers an introduction to studying the ancient past.

covers.courses/SLL1101F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 249 (Language options row 12)

rows.printed:
SLL1101F Xhosa Communication IA
Course outline: This course takes students from zero knowledge of Xhosa to a good, basic competency in the language.
The course actively engages students in acquiring the language through a series of well-developed
modules with an integrated approach to acquiring speaking, writing and comprehension skills in
Xhosa. Grammar is taught in context and students are expected to apply their grammatical knowledge
in task-based communication situations. Students are taught about different varieties of Xhosa and
how to use these appropriately in social contexts.
Entry requirements: None. This is a course for beginners. Students with an Nguni language
as a 1st language are not permitted to do this course and are encouraged to register for SLL1131F
isiXhosa Language & Literature Studies IA.
Class times: Monday to Friday 3rd period.
Assessment: Year work (tests, assignments and portfolio activities) counts 35%; orals count 15%;
one two-hour examination counts 50% of the final mark.

DP requirements: Students are expected to complete all tests and assignments and attend at least
80% of all lectures, tutorials and language labs.
Other details: None

new.summary: The course takes beginners from no Xhosa to basic competency through modules combining speaking, writing and comprehension. Grammar is taught in context, as students practise tasks and learn to use Xhosa varieties appropriately in social settings.

covers.courses/SLL1102S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 249–250 (Language options row 13)

rows.printed:
SLL1102S Xhosa Communication IB
Course outline: This course is a continuation of SLL1101F. On completion of this course, students would have
covered more complex conversational and grammatical structures, enabling them to engage in a wide
range of meaningful communicative activities. Students begin to read a simple Xhosa text and to
increase their vocabularies by working with words relating to particular domains and tasks with
contemporary, local and cultural significance.
Entry requirements: SLL1101F or SLL1018S, or equivalent at the discretion of the Head of
Section. Students with a Nguni language as a 1 st language are not permitted to do this course and are
encouraged to register for SLL1132S isiXhosa Language & Literature Studies IB.
Class times: Monday to Friday 3rd period.
Assessment: Year work (tests, assignments and portfolio activities) counts 35%; orals count 15%;
one two-hour examination counts 50% of the final mark.

DP requirements: Students are expected to complete all tests and assignments and attend at least
80% of all lectures, tutorials and language labs.
Other details: None

new.summary: Students build on earlier Xhosa study, learning more complex conversational and grammatical structures for wider communication. They begin reading simple Xhosa texts and expand vocabulary through contemporary, local and culturally significant domains and tasks.

covers.courses/SLL1117S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 245 (Language options row 5)

rows.printed:
SLL1117S Swahili Communication 1B
Course outline: In continuity with the foundational beginners course (SLL1017F/S), this course provides more basic
knowledge on Swahili grammar, especially on Swahili derivations and skills on simple spoken and
written Swahili. This will enable the student to participate in more advanced communication in
Swahili. Moreover, it provides more cultural notes in the use of Swahili according to specific contexts
introduced.
Entry requirements: SLL1017F/S
Class times: Monday to Friday, 6th period.
Assessment: Coursework (tests, assignments and portfolio activities) count 35%; orals count 15%;
one two-hour examination counts 50% of the final mark.

DP requirements: Students are expected to complete all tests and assignments and attend at least
80% of all lectures, tutorials and language labs.
Other details: None

new.summary: This course builds on beginner Swahili, covering more grammar, especially word derivations, and developing simple spoken and written communication. Students learn to participate in more advanced Swahili communication and gain cultural guidance on using the language in different contexts.

covers.courses/SLL1121F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 259 (Language options row 20)

rows.printed:
SLL1121F Chinese Studies IA
Course outline: This Chinese language course is designed for non-mother tongue students who wish to acquire
essential communicative skills in both spoken and written Chinese through a combination of lectures,
conversation classes and language laboratory sessions. No prior knowledge of the Chinese language
is needed when the students are enrolled into the course, which is designed as an academic course that
builds up the foundation for Chinese studies in later stages. The first year course covers a sizeable
repertoire of Chinese characters as used in everyday communicative situations, and develops an
awareness and understanding of the cultural aspects of the unique Chinese writing system. By the end
of the course, students are expected to be able to make simple conversations in Chinese on some
specific everyday situations.
Entry requirements: None. This is a course designed for beginners.
Class times: Monday to Friday 4th period.
Assessment: Coursework (assignments and tests) counts for 40% of the final mark; two-hour written
examination counts for 40%; oral and aural examination counts for 20%.

DP requirements: Students must attend classes, lab sessions and tutorials regularly, submit the
prescribed number of assignments and write any class test that may be scheduled. Submission dates
must be adhered to.
Other details: None

new.summary: This beginner course builds essential spoken and written Chinese through lectures, conversation classes and language laboratory sessions. You learn everyday characters, explore cultural aspects of Chinese writing, and practise simple conversations in everyday situations.

covers.courses/SLL1122S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 259–260 (Language options row 21)

rows.printed:
SLL1122S Chinese Studies IB
Course outline: The course is a continuation of SLL1121F, and through a combination of lectures, conversation classes
and language laboratory sessions, it aims to further develop communicative competence in aural
comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing of modern Chinese. Students are expected to be able
to read and understand the texts in Chinese characters instead of relying on pinyin that is now merely
used as an aid for looking up characters in dictionaries and getting the pronunciation of characters
correct. By the end of the course learners should be able to write short paragraphs in characters, in
addition to being able to talk about daily life events.
Entry requirements: SLL1121F, or equivalent at the discretion of the Head of Section.
Class times: Monday to Friday 4th period.
Assessment: Coursework (assignments and tests) counts for 40% of the final mark; two-hour written
examination counts for 40%; oral and aural examination counts for 20%.

DP requirements: Students must attend classes, lab sessions and tutorials regularly, submit the
prescribed number of assignments and write any class test that may be scheduled. Submission dates
must be adhered to.
Other details: None

new.summary: This course develops Chinese listening, speaking, reading and writing through lectures, conversation classes and language laboratory sessions. You practise reading Chinese characters and learn to write short paragraphs and talk about everyday events.

covers.courses/SLL1131F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 251 (Language options row 14)

rows.printed:
SLL1131F isiXhosa Language & Literature Studies IA
Course outline: The course introduces students to isiXhosa language, literacy and culture. It examines the
contributions of isiXhosa linguistic and cultural competence to multilingualism discourses through an
examination of language in context, literary discourse, language and society and translation studies.
The main focus at this level is on developing writing skills such as awareness of orthographic changes
and spelling conventions, academic writing, and language policy issues such as standardisation,
dialects and the impact on education.
Entry requirements: The student must have passed an African language (isiXhosa, isiZulu,
isiNdebele, isiSwati) at Grade 12 level or have completed SLL1101F Xhosa Communication IA and
SLL1102S Xhosa Communication IB.
Class times: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday 2nd period.
Assessment: Year work (tests, assignments and projects) 50%, one two-hour examination 50%.

DP requirements: Students are expected to attend 80% of all lectures and tutorials and to complete
all tests, projects and assignments.
Other details: None

new.summary: Students explore isiXhosa language, literacy and culture through language in context, literature, society and translation. They develop academic writing skills and examine spelling conventions, standardisation, dialects and language policy in education.

covers.courses/SLL1132S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 251–252 (Language options row 15)

rows.printed:
SLL1132S isiXhosa Language & Literature Studies IB
Course outline: This course is a continuation of SLL1131F. The course further develops students’ isiXhosa linguistic
skills and cultural competence and literacy. The approach in this course is to discuss topics of language
development and apply them to specific areas of language policy and planning. We also explore the
role of African languages under the topics of language and power.
Entry requirements: SLL1131F isiXhosa Language and Literature Studies IA.
Class times: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday 2nd period.
Assessment: Year work (tests, assignments and projects) 50%, one two-hour examination 50%.

DP requirements: Students are expected to attend 80% of all lectures and tutorials and to complete
all tests, projects and assignments.
Other details: None

new.summary: The course further develops isiXhosa language skills, cultural competence and literacy, exploring language development and applying it to language policy and planning. You also examine the role of African languages through language and power.

covers.courses/SLL1136S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 269 (Courses row 67)

rows.printed:
SLL1136S Introduction to Roman Literature and Culture
Course outline: This course provides an introduction to the cultural history of ancient Rome and her empire. The
Aeneid, the poet Virgil's epic account of Rome's origins and of the vision of her later greatness, will
form a starting point for a survey of Roman culture through ancient texts (in translation), art and
archaeology. Students will acquire basic familiarity with the most significant Roman literary genres,
and with the study of Roman life and society.
Entry requirements: None
Class times: 6th period.
Assessment: Coursework (2 essays [chosen from 3 options] and 2 tutorial assignments); compulsory
attendance of tutorials – 50%. Formal examination at the end of the semester – 50%.

DP requirements: Timely submission of all coursework as stipulated in the Classics Section’s
handbook.
Other details: None

new.summary: Explore ancient Rome and its empire through Virgil’s Aeneid, an epic of Rome’s origins, plus ancient texts in translation, art and archaeology. You’ll learn key Roman literary genres and about studying Roman life and society.

covers.courses/SLL2058F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 269–270 (Courses row 68)

rows.printed:
SLL2058F Ancient Mythology
Course outline: This course provides an introduction to Greek mythology and concepts of the divine, followed by a
detailed study of selected myths of Ancient Greece and Rome, including the following topics:
Theories of Myths and their meaning; the ideological uses of Myth; Myth in Classical Art and
literature; Myth in post-classical literary and artistic traditions.
Entry requirements: 2nd year status
Class times: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday 4th period.
Assessment: One two-hour examination in June counts for 50% of the final mark; coursework counts
for 50%.

DP requirements: Students must attend classes regularly, submit the prescribed number of essays
and assignments and write any class test that may be scheduled. Submission dates must be adhered to.
Other details: None

new.summary: Explore Greek and Roman myths and ideas about the divine, considering theories of myth, what myths mean, and how they have been used ideologically. Study myth in classical art and literature, and its later literary and artistic traditions.

covers.courses/SOC1001F: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 400–401 (Courses row 69)

rows.printed:
SOC1001F Introduction to Sociology
Course outline: People move through life in a set of socially structured institutions like the family, education, work
and eldership. How are we shaped by the society around us? What part can we play in shaping our
society? How have sociologists tried to make sense of the society around us in which our everyday
experience is located? What is the sociological imagination? How does it help us to go beneath surface
appearances to better understand what is happening? The course introduces students to major ways in
which sociologists have grappled to make sense of historically dynamic society in an increasingly
globalised context.
Entry requirements: None
Class times: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday 4th or 6th period.
Assessment: Continuous assessment (essays, projects, tests, etc.) counts 100%.

DP requirements: Completion of all written tests, essays and assignments.
Other details: None

new.summary: Explore how family, education, work and other institutions shape everyday life, and how people can shape society. Learn how sociologists use the sociological imagination to look beneath appearances and understand society in a globalised world.

covers.courses/SOC1005S: UCT Faculty of Humanities Undergraduate Handbook 2026 (Book 9a), p. 401 (Courses row 70)

rows.printed:
SOC1005S Individual and Society
Course outline: This is an introductory course, designed to explore key issues and activities in South African society
today. It aims to assist the student to search for and identify accurate information and relevant ideas,
situate these in social context, and to outline and begin to probe views around key social issues. We
live in a society with deeply structured social inequalities and a range of issues and problems which
people confront every day. What is actually happening to people positioned differently in society?
What is changing and what is continuing? How do ordinary people deal with these issues? What forms
of organisation and action do they turn to as they try to meet their needs and build lives which are
fulfilling and dignified? The course examines selected social processes, structures, institutions and
behaviours which help us understand these issues and ways of dealing with them.
Entry requirements: None
Class times: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday 4th or 6th period.
Assessment: Continuous assessment (essays, projects, tests, etc.) counts 100%.

DP requirements: Completion of all written tests, essays and assignments as set.
Other details: This course may also be offered in Summer Term - please consult the department.

new.summary: Explore key issues in contemporary South African society, including structured inequalities and how social processes, institutions and behaviours shape people's experiences. Consider what changes, what persists, and how people organise and act to meet needs.
